cards.title: Nonresident attorney
cards.front: What permits the ordinary nonresident route?
cards.rule: Ohio Supreme Court admission and the principal-business or primary-practice connection specified by statute.
cards.boundary: Online authority has separate Ohio residence and location conditions.
cards.mixup: An ordinary nonresident exception is not permission for out-of-state RON.

cards.title: Attorney initial learning
cards.front: What applies to an Ohio attorney first applying after September 20, 2019?
cards.rule: The ordinary course is required and ordinary test is exempted.
cards.boundary: RON has separate learning and testing.
cards.mixup: An ordinary test exemption does not remove the course.

cards.title: Continuing attorney term
cards.front: When does ordinary attorney authority continue?
cards.rule: While the statutory Ohio connection, good standing and no-revocation conditions hold.
cards.boundary: It is distinct from the ordinary five-year nonattorney term.
cards.mixup: Continuing authority is not unconditional lifetime immunity.

cards.title: Attorney online clock
cards.front: How long does attorney RON authorization last?
cards.rule: Until the earlier of five years or the end of ordinary notarial authority.
cards.boundary: The online renewal window has its own expiration reference.
cards.mixup: An ongoing ordinary term does not make RON permanent.

cards.title: Privileged journal access
cards.front: Who can request an attorney-online-notary entry under the special ordinary-access rule?
cards.rule: A principal or someone acting on the principal's behalf, with the stated privilege protection.
cards.boundary: Official examination has a separate privilege-objection provision.
cards.mixup: A stranger's curiosity does not open the attorney's entire journal.

cards.title: Jurat elements
cards.front: What does a jurat require?
cards.rule: Appearance, the administered oath or affirmation, and signing in the notary's presence.
cards.boundary: The certificate accurately describes those completed elements.
cards.mixup: Silent witnessing is not administration of a truth pledge.

cards.title: Secular pledge
cards.front: What alternative to religious swearing is recognized?
cards.rule: An affirmation under penalty of perjury with the required truth commitment.
cards.boundary: Substantially similar statutory-question wording is permitted.
cards.mixup: A secular pledge does not remove truth accountability.

cards.title: Act and certificate
cards.front: Which certificate follows the truth pledge?
cards.rule: Use the certificate corresponding to the actual sworn or affirmed act.
cards.boundary: Acknowledgment and jurat certificates are not interchanged across unperformed procedures.
cards.mixup: The record's title cannot supply a missing oath.

cards.title: Explain without selecting
cards.front: What can a nonattorney explain?
cards.rule: The procedural difference between acknowledgment and jurat.
cards.boundary: Do not advise which act best suits the legal situation under this section.
cards.mixup: A procedural explanation does not become a legal selection opinion.

cards.title: Wrong-act certificate
cards.front: What response is required when a certificate misidentifies the act?
cards.rule: Provide a correct certificate at no charge.
cards.boundary: The completed-original alteration prohibition is separately observed.
cards.mixup: A correction fee does not authorize pen edits to a completed certificate.

cards.title: Direct copy claims
cards.front: Which ordinary assertions are prohibited for the notary?
cards.rule: Direct certification that a document is an original or a true copy of another record.
cards.boundary: Specific statutory routes have their own conditions.
cards.mixup: A perfect photocopy alone does not confer ordinary copy-certification power.

cards.title: Holder statement
cards.front: What does the holder-signature provision preserve?
cards.rule: Notarization of the holder's signature on the holder's written copy-certification statement.
cards.boundary: The notary performs the chosen lawful signature procedure.
cards.mixup: The holder's assertion does not become the notary's direct copy guarantee.

cards.title: Journal-copy exception
cards.front: What special copy can an online notary certify?
cards.rule: Copies from the online notary's own electronic journal under the section.
cards.boundary: The request and limited-entry access conditions remain applicable.
cards.mixup: The exception does not authorize every private-record copy.

cards.title: Printed electronic record
cards.front: What supports the particular printed-record acceptance route?
cards.rule: The attached authenticator certificate in the stated or substantially similar format.
cards.boundary: The authenticator supplies the reproduction assertion and sworn execution.
cards.mixup: This route is not a general expansion of ordinary notary copy power.

cards.title: Authenticator format exception
cards.front: How is the authenticator certificate executed?
cards.rule: It cannot be signed or notarized with electronic signature or seal, including RON.
cards.boundary: The electronic source does not remove this specific restriction.
cards.mixup: A remote convenience request does not waive the paper-execution boundary.

cards.title: Blank records
cards.front: When is the document too incomplete?
cards.rule: Do not notarize a signature on a blank or incomplete document.
cards.boundary: Do not deliver pre-signed blank affidavit or acknowledgment forms for later use.
cards.mixup: A customer's promise to fill fields later does not complete the record now.

cards.title: After signing
cards.front: Can the notary edit signed instrument terms?
cards.rule: The statute prohibits altering a written instrument after anyone has signed it.
cards.boundary: Completed certificates also have their own alteration prohibition.
cards.mixup: A recipient request does not create edit authority.

cards.title: Current capacity
cards.front: What condition prevents proceeding?
cards.rule: Do not notarize where the signer appears unable to understand the record's nature and effect.
cards.boundary: The statute separately addresses a removed right after court adjudication.
cards.mixup: A clear ID does not establish legal understanding.

cards.title: Free will
cards.front: What influence concern matters?
cards.rule: Apparent coercion or undue influence compromising free will prevents notarization.
cards.boundary: The notary evaluates the actual signing situation.
cards.mixup: A companion's urgency is not voluntary execution.

cards.title: Certificate contents
cards.front: What identifies the actual event?
cards.rule: Venue, wording, date, exact signature, printed name, seal and expiration, with electronic-method statement when applicable.
cards.boundary: A certificate may be attached separately through the permitted form options.
cards.mixup: A bare official seal is not the complete certificate.

cards.title: Ordinary ceiling
cards.front: What is the basic non-online maximum?
cards.rule: Five dollars per notarial act under the current statute.
cards.boundary: The basic fees are not calculated by signature.
cards.mixup: Multiple signatures do not automatically multiply the fee.

cards.title: Online ceiling
cards.front: What is the current online basic maximum?
cards.rule: Thirty dollars.
cards.boundary: Do not add the ordinary basic fee to the online basic fee.
cards.mixup: An older twenty-five-dollar figure does not match the opened current statute.

cards.title: Travel agreement
cards.front: What supports a travel fee?
cards.rule: A reasonable fee agreed by notary and principal before the act.
cards.boundary: It is separate from the basic statutory fee structure.
cards.mixup: Surprise travel billing misses the advance agreement condition.

cards.title: Technology unit
cards.front: How is the technology cap applied?
cards.rule: Up to ten dollars total per online session.
cards.boundary: The fee may apply even if identification failure prevents completion.
cards.mixup: Each attempted quiz does not create a fresh ten-dollar unit.

cards.title: Separate invoice categories
cards.front: Which categories may coexist?
cards.rule: The appropriate basic fee and lawful additional travel or technology charges under their own conditions.
cards.boundary: Ordinary and online basic fees cannot both be stacked for the act.
cards.mixup: Provider training fees are not customer notarial fees.

cards.title: Representative acknowledgment
cards.front: What does the representative declare?
cards.rule: Proper authority and execution as the represented person's or entity's act for the stated purpose.
cards.boundary: The human representative is identified.
cards.mixup: A company title alone does not identify the appearing individual.

cards.title: Corporation and LLC
cards.front: What facts connect entity execution?
cards.rule: Identify the appearing officer, agent, member or manager and the represented entity in the applicable form.
cards.boundary: The statutory meaning includes proper authority and entity purpose.
cards.mixup: The acknowledgment does not guarantee solvency.

cards.title: Attorney-in-fact roles
cards.front: Who appears in the agency acknowledgment?
cards.rule: The attorney-in-fact acknowledges execution for the principal.
cards.boundary: The form distinguishes the agent and principal.
cards.mixup: Attorney-in-fact status is not admission to practice law.

cards.title: Legal validity limit
cards.front: What is outside the nonattorney notary determination?
cards.rule: Do not determine legal validity of a power of attorney or other representative-capacity form under this subsection.
cards.boundary: The statutory exception concerns an Ohio-licensed attorney.
cards.mixup: Recording the acknowledgment is not a legal opinion that the authority document is valid.

cards.title: Interest screening
cards.front: What conflicts matter?
cards.rule: A direct financial or other interest beyond authorized fees and the listed named-party capacities.
cards.boundary: An entity role can be relevant to a notary's own conflict.
cards.mixup: A fee waiver does not remove an actual trustee or party role.

cards.title: Online identity
cards.front: Which unknown-principal route is specified?
cards.rule: Unexpired government photo-and-signature credential, remote presentation, analysis and proofing.
cards.boundary: Personal knowledge and the qualifying single credible witness are alternative routes.
cards.mixup: A private email profile does not complete the prescribed evidence.

cards.title: Session restart
cards.front: What follows a broken link or compromised session?
cards.rule: Restart identity authentication and incomplete acts from the beginning.
cards.boundary: The rule also covers a participant exiting the session.
cards.mixup: A fee payment does not allow skipping the restart.

cards.title: Journal privacy
cards.front: What sensitive number is excluded?
cards.rule: Do not enter social security numbers in the electronic journal.
cards.boundary: Record the actual identity evidence under the permitted fields.
cards.mixup: A longer entry is not automatically a better compliant entry.

cards.title: End-of-term journal
cards.front: What happens when online authority expires?
cards.rule: Transfer the journal to the Secretary or approved repository under the statute, with the required location information.
cards.boundary: The receiver has the stated ten-year duty and renewed authority starts a new journal.
cards.mixup: Subscription cancellation does not authorize archive deletion.

cards.title: Personal credential control
cards.front: Who may use the electronic signature and seal?
cards.rule: Only the named notary for authorized notarial purposes.
cards.boundary: Secure control and statutory incident notice continue when using third-party storage.
cards.mixup: A shared employer login does not grant shared notarial authority.

cards.title: Approval and oath
cards.front: What precedes official work after approval?
cards.rule: Personally appear before a notary or other authorized officer for the office oath.
cards.boundary: The SOS process places this before performing duties.
cards.mixup: An approval email does not administer the oath.

cards.title: Oath officer
cards.front: Who can administer the office oath?
cards.rule: A notary or another officer authorized by law to administer oaths.
cards.boundary: Actual personal appearance is required by the provision.
cards.mixup: The applicant cannot replace this with a self-administered promise.

cards.title: Seal preparation
cards.front: What supply precedes duties?
cards.rule: Obtain the official Ohio seal.
cards.boundary: The state coat-of-arms circle and surrounding contents follow the statute.
cards.mixup: A private course badge is not the official seal.

cards.title: Name location
cards.front: Must the name always be built into the seal?
cards.rule: The statute permits legible printed, typed or stamped name near the signature instead.
cards.boundary: Other required seal contents remain.
cards.mixup: The alternative does not permit omitting every identifying fact.

cards.title: Prior seal continuation
cards.front: Which older seal has special treatment?
cards.rule: The qualifying compliant seal possessed before September 20, 2019 by the then-commissioned person.
cards.boundary: The grandfather rule does not extend a commission's legal term.
cards.mixup: A newly purchased deficient seal is not grandfathered by preference.

cards.title: Ordinary renewal window
cards.front: When can renewal begin?
cards.rule: Three months before commission expiration.
cards.boundary: If expiration precedes filing, apply for a new commission under the section.
cards.mixup: A pending plan does not extend authority.

cards.title: Ordinary CE
cards.front: What is required for nonattorney renewal?
cards.rule: One authorized education hour and no test under the current SOS table.
cards.boundary: The rule supplies the applicable recency period.
cards.mixup: Do not reuse the three-hour initial route for every renewal.

cards.title: Online CE
cards.front: What is the online renewal learning requirement?
cards.rule: One approved hour and no test under the current table.
cards.boundary: It is separate from any ordinary renewal requirement.
cards.mixup: An ongoing attorney commission does not remove online renewal.

cards.title: Contact and resignation
cards.front: What must reach the Secretary?
cards.rule: Prescribed notice within thirty days for legal name/address changes and a resignation notice with effective date when resigning.
cards.boundary: Electronic-submission requirements apply.
cards.mixup: Postal forwarding is not the state record update.

cards.title: Expired authority
cards.front: Can a known expired commission support one favor?
cards.rule: The chapter prohibits knowingly acting after expiration or resignation.
cards.boundary: A validity-saving provision concerns a different legal effect.
cards.mixup: An old stamp or free service does not renew authority.

application.summary: The ordinary Ohio first route combines eligibility, a recent BCI report, authorized education and testing, and electronic filing.

sections.heading: Prepare the evidence
sections.body: Meet age eighteen and the ordinary Ohio legal-residence condition unless the specified attorney alternative applies. A nonexempt applicant submits a BCI report within the preceding six months. The initial nonattorney course is three hours with the authorized provider's test. The SOS page calls for education within twelve months before application and identifies completion evidence for upload.

sections.heading: File the complete application
sections.body: Upload the signature sample, required background report and provider proof through the official online system. Provider education fees and state filing fees are separate. The ordinary retake waits at least thirty days and stays within the BCI-based outer window. A second failure requires the restart described by rule. Approval is followed by the office oath before work.

example.heading: A report near expiration
example.body: A Cleveland applicant studies after receiving a BCI report. A failed test means the applicant checks both the thirty-day waiting period and the six-month report clock before booking a retake. The course receipt does not refresh the older report.

keyFacts: Ordinary initial nonattorneys take three hours and a test.
The BCI report has its own six-month window.
State applications are electronic.

attorney-exception.summary: Ohio attorneys have specific ordinary exceptions, while online authority keeps separate residence, term and learning conditions.

sections.heading: Apply the actual ordinary exception
sections.body: An Ohio-admitted attorney can use the specified principal-business or primary-practice connection while nonresident. Ohio attorneys are exempt from the application BCI check. First commissioning after September 20, 2019 still requires the ordinary course but no ordinary test. The earlier commissioned attorney category has its stated education and test exception.

sections.heading: Track online duties separately
sections.body: Ordinary attorney authority continues only while the statutory Ohio connection, good standing and no-revocation conditions hold. RON still needs separate authorization and learning, and the online officer is an Ohio resident physically in Ohio. Attorney online authorization expires at the earlier of five years or the ordinary term ending. Attorney online-journal access also has principal and privilege safeguards.

example.heading: A border-state law office
example.body: An Ohio-admitted attorney lives in Kentucky and has a primary Ohio practice. That can satisfy the ordinary connection alternative. It does not satisfy the separate Ohio-resident condition for online notarization, so the attorney does not treat ordinary eligibility as remote authorization.

keyFacts: Attorney ordinary test exemption does not waive every course.
Ordinary attorney authority depends on continuing conditions.
Attorney RON has a separate five-year limit.

oath.summary: An Ohio jurat requires actual oath or affirmation and signing in the notary's presence. Its certificate describes that procedure.

sections.heading: Administer the truth pledge
sections.body: Identify the lawful appearance and administer the statutory or substantially similar truth question. A signer may affirm under penalty of perjury without religious swearing. The signer makes the pledge about the document and signs in the notary's presence. Silent observation or a document heading cannot perform these elements.

sections.heading: Match the written evidence
sections.body: Use a jurat only when the oath or affirmation actually occurred, and avoid acknowledgment in place of a required pledge. A nonattorney may explain the procedural difference but does not choose the act best suited to the customer's legal situation. A wrong-act certificate requires a correct certificate at no charge while the completed-original alteration prohibition remains applicable.

example.heading: An unsigned truth declaration
example.body: A Dayton customer is willing to affirm truth but has brought an earlier signed document. The notary completes the requested lawful jurat procedure, including present signing, instead of assuming the existing signature alone completes every element. The certificate reflects the actual oath event.

keyFacts: A jurat includes appearance, pledge and present signing.
Affirmation is a recognized alternative.
Certificate wording follows the act actually performed.

copy-limits.summary: Ohio distinguishes prohibited direct copy certification from a holder's notarized statement and specific statutory journal or authenticator routes.

sections.heading: Keep the assertion with its maker
sections.body: The ordinary notary does not directly certify that a document is an original or true copy. Section 147.141(B) preserves notarizing the holder's signature on the holder's written copy-accuracy statement. The chosen signature act still requires its normal procedure. The notary does not convert that act into a personal guarantee of the copied record.

sections.heading: Use specific exceptions within scope
sections.body: An online notary can certify copies from the officer's own electronic journal under the section and its access conditions. Section 147.591 separately gives an authenticator-certificate route for printed electronically executed documents. The authenticator makes the reproduction assertion and the certificate cannot be signed or notarized with electronic signature or seal, including RON.

example.heading: A holder brings a private copy
example.body: A Toledo holder writes and signs a sworn statement about their copy. The notary administers the lawful requested signature act. A separate request for the notary's own direct true-copy certificate remains outside ordinary power. The identity of the person making the copy assertion matters.

keyFacts: Ordinary direct original/true-copy certification is prohibited.
Holder-signature notarization is expressly preserved.
The authenticator certificate has a paper-execution restriction.

incomplete-records.summary: Ohio prohibits notarizing blank or incomplete records and limits changes after signing or completed notarization.

sections.heading: Pause for the actual document and signer
sections.body: The notary does not notarize a signature on a blank or incomplete document or deliver a signed blank certificate for later use. Apparent inability to understand nature and effect, or coercion compromising free will, prevents the stated act. A clear ID does not establish document completion or voluntary understanding.

sections.heading: Preserve accurate completed evidence
sections.body: Do not alter the signed instrument or amend a completed certificate under the prohibited-acts section. Every act needs the completed certificate with actual venue, wording, date, commissioned signature, printed name, seal and expiration, plus the applicable electronic-method statement. The correct-certificate duty for a wrong-act form is distinct from permission to edit an original.

example.heading: A pressured blank agreement
example.body: At a Columbus office, a companion urges immediate signing while substantive terms remain empty. The notary resolves neither problem by collecting the fee or applying a legible seal. The incomplete-record and free-will conditions both require attention before a lawful act.

keyFacts: Substantive blanks cannot be cured by a promise to fill later.
Signed instruments and completed certificates have alteration prohibitions.
Certificate contents describe the actual event.

ordinary-fees.summary: Ohio's current statute uses separate basic ordinary and online fee ceilings, with additional travel and technology conditions.

sections.heading: Use the correct unit
sections.body: The ordinary non-online ceiling is five dollars and the online basic ceiling is thirty. The two basic categories cannot be stacked for the same online act, and the statutory basic fee is not calculated per signature. A provider's education charge is a different fee from the notarial service received by a customer.

sections.heading: Apply additional charges correctly
sections.body: A reasonable travel fee is agreed with the principal before the act. The online technology fee is capped at ten dollars total per session and can apply despite noncompletion, including identity-process failure. Several attempts in one session do not create a fresh cap for every question or retry. Overcharging or accepting an excessive act fee is prohibited.

example.heading: An online invoice with two basics
example.body: An Akron online invoice lists thirty dollars online basic, five dollars ordinary basic and a lawful capped technology charge. The added ordinary basic conflicts with the no-stacking rule. The technology charge is assessed under its own statutory conditions.

keyFacts: Ordinary basic maximum is five dollars.
Online basic maximum is thirty dollars.
Technology is at most ten dollars per online session.

representative-capacity.summary: Ohio acknowledgment identifies the human representative and their execution for the represented principal or entity.

sections.heading: Describe the representative act
sections.body: Corporate officers, LLC members or managers, partners, attorneys-in-fact and other representatives have specific statutory acknowledgment meanings and short forms. They acknowledge proper authority and execution for the represented party and stated purpose. Identity assurance remains necessary even where the certificate lists an impressive title.

sections.heading: Keep legal opinions separate
sections.body: A nonattorney notary does not determine legal validity of the power of attorney or other representative-capacity form under section 147.141(A)(17). The representative's acknowledgment of authority is distinct from the notary issuing a legal opinion on that source of authority. The notary also screens their own named-party or direct-interest conflict.

example.heading: An agent and a power document
example.body: A Cincinnati attorney-in-fact appears with a power document. The notary identifies the agent and records the proper representative acknowledgment. A request to guarantee the power's legal validity calls for an authority the nonattorney notary does not acquire through this ceremony.

keyFacts: The human representative appears and is identified.
The certificate reflects the represented role.
Nonattorney authority does not include a legal-validity opinion.

remote-authorization.summary: Ohio online work requires separate state authorization, compliant technology and secure records under the current statute and rules.

sections.heading: Qualify and conduct the session
sections.body: Hold ordinary authority, meet Ohio residency, complete the RON course and test and obtain written authorization. The online officer is physically in Ohio. Use personal knowledge or the prescribed identity route, adequate live two-way audiovisual technology, matching electronic document and tamper-evident execution. A broken or compromised session triggers restarting identity authentication and incomplete acts.

sections.heading: Secure the record lifecycle
sections.body: Keep chronological tamper-evident authenticated electronic journals with the required participant, record, location, system and fee information. Exclude social security numbers. Preserve required audiovisual records and backups under personal control, with compliant third-party storage if used. Expiration transfer, approved repository retention and a new journal on renewal have separate statutory steps. Credentials and incident reports follow section 147.66.

example.heading: A successful proofing result before disconnection
example.body: An Ohio principal passes the identity process, then the link breaks before completion. Reconnection does not permit simply stamping the record. The rule requires restarting identity authentication and incomplete acts from the beginning, with the actual lawful session recorded and entered.

keyFacts: The online notary resides and acts physically in Ohio.
A proofing result does not replace the remaining act.
Records and credentials have separate security and transfer duties.

oath-of-office.summary: An Ohio appointee takes the office oath after approval and before entering upon duties.

sections.heading: Appear before an authorized officer
sections.body: The current SOS sequence places the oath after application approval. The appointee personally appears before a notary or another officer authorized by law to administer oaths. A self-signed promise or saved approval email does not administer the required oath. It is separate from a customer's later jurat or the RON identity quiz.

sections.heading: Prepare the official execution supply
sections.body: Before duties, obtain the Ohio seal with its prescribed coat-of-arms circle and surrounding information. The statute allows the notary's name to be supplied legibly near the signature rather than built into the seal. The specified grandfather provision concerns a previously compliant seal already possessed by a person commissioned before the cutoff, and does not extend authority's term.

example.heading: Approval on a busy morning
example.body: An approved appointee receives a first customer request before taking the oath. The appointee arranges the personal oath before a legally authorized officer and obtains the required seal before working. A customer deadline does not move the oath after the first act.

keyFacts: Approval precedes the office oath in the current process.
The oath precedes official duties.
Another legally authorized oath officer can administer it.

renewal.summary: Ohio ordinary and online renewals have separate windows and continuing education rules. Expiration before filing changes the route.

sections.heading: Prepare within the window
sections.body: Ordinary nonattorney authority lasts five years unless revoked. Renewal opens three months before expiration and needs the applicable new BCI report and application. The current education table uses one ordinary approved hour with no test. Online renewal separately uses one approved hour with no test and its own authorization date, including for attorneys.

sections.heading: Handle expiration and official changes
sections.body: If the commission expires before renewal submission, apply for a new commission under the section. Known expiration or resignation bars further acts, even though a separate provision addresses validity of acts already performed. Report legal name or address changes within thirty days and resignation through the prescribed effective-date notice. Cooperation with lawful investigation remains required.

example.heading: A late renewal filing
example.body: A Springfield nonattorney discovers expiration before submitting the renewal. The statute directs the new-commission route. The person does not perform a free favor with the expired seal while preparing the application, because pending plans do not restore current authority.

keyFacts: Ordinary renewal opens three months before expiration.
Ordinary nonattorney renewal uses one hour and no test.
Expiration before submission leads to a new application route.

articles.keyword: Ohio copy statements require the right person making the assertion
articles.title: Ohio copy statements require the right person making the assertion
articles.description: Distinguish a holder statement, a journal copy and the printed-electronic-record route.
articles.h1: Ohio copy statements require the right person making the assertion
articles.lede: A request for a certified copy can describe several legally different Ohio procedures.

sections.heading: Start with ordinary authority
sections.body: A Columbus customer asks the notary to certify a private photocopy as true to its original. Section 147.141 prohibits the ordinary notary from directly certifying either original status or a true copy. Comparing pages carefully does not by itself confer that notarial power. The request must be examined before adding a certificate that makes the notary the person asserting copy accuracy.

sections.heading: Identify a holder statement
sections.body: The same section preserves notarizing the signature of the document holder on a written statement that the copy is true. The holder makes that assertion. The notary completes the actual requested lawful signature act, including oath and present signing if a jurat is requested. The resulting notarization does not silently convert the holder's statement into the notary's own direct guarantee.

sections.heading: Read the specific exceptions
sections.body: An online notary may certify copies from their own electronic journal under section 147.65, subject to the access conditions. That exception concerns a particular notarial record. Section 147.591 separately provides an attached authenticator certificate for the stated printed-electronic-document acceptance route. Each provision has a defined role rather than creating universal ordinary copy authority.

sections.heading: Use the authenticator's proper format
sections.body: In the printed-electronic route, the authenticator supplies the reproduction warranty and the notary administers its sworn execution. The authenticator certificate may not be signed or notarized with electronic signature or seal, including RON. A record that began electronically therefore can have a paper-execution condition at this specific later certification stage.

faqs.q: Does the holder's statement make the notary the copy certifier?
faqs.a: No. The holder supplies that assertion and the notary performs the signature act.

faqs.q: Can the authenticator certificate use RON?
faqs.a: Section 147.591(C) prohibits electronic signing or notarization of that certificate.

articles.keyword: Ohio's wrong-act certificate remedy differs from editing a completed original
articles.title: Ohio's wrong-act certificate remedy differs from editing a completed original
articles.description: Read the correct-certificate duty alongside the alteration prohibition.
articles.h1: Ohio's wrong-act certificate remedy differs from editing a completed original
articles.lede: An Ohio certificate must describe the actual acknowledgment or sworn procedure that occurred.

sections.heading: Examine the actual act
sections.body: At a Dayton appointment, the signer takes the required affirmation and signs in the notary's presence, but the notary supplies an acknowledgment certificate. The written evidence does not match the performed sworn procedure. Ohio expressly prohibits using acknowledgment evidence where an oath or affirmation was administered and a jurat where it was not.

sections.heading: Provide the stated remedy
sections.body: Section 147.542 requires a correct certificate at no charge when the certificate incorrectly indicates the type of notarization performed. This duty addresses the evidence the signer receives. It is important to establish which act actually occurred before preparing the correct evidence, because a replacement cannot truthfully claim an oath that was never administered.

sections.heading: Respect the completed-original restriction
sections.body: The prohibited-acts section separately bars amending or altering a notarial certificate after completion and altering a written instrument after anyone signed it. A request to cross out wording on the completed original must therefore be distinguished from the statutory duty to supply a correct certificate. A paid correction charge cannot create authority to ignore those limits.

sections.heading: Keep procedure advice in its scope
sections.body: The nonattorney may explain how acknowledgment and jurat procedures differ but does not advise which best fits the customer's legal situation. If the original event itself lacked a required element, an accurate account of the facts remains essential. The certificate is evidence of an act and cannot manufacture an unperformed truth pledge or missing appearance.

faqs.q: Is the correct certificate charged to the signer?
faqs.a: The statute requires it at no charge for a wrong-type certificate.

faqs.q: Can a certificate create an oath that never occurred?
faqs.a: No. It must accurately evidence the actual lawful act.

articles.keyword: Ohio attorney authority has a separate online residence test
articles.title: Ohio attorney authority has a separate online residence test
articles.description: Track ordinary eligibility, continuing term and five-year online authorization independently.
articles.h1: Ohio attorney authority has a separate online residence test
articles.lede: A nonresident attorney can meet one ordinary exception while failing a separate RON condition.

sections.heading: Identify the ordinary connection
sections.body: An attorney lives in Kentucky, is admitted by the Ohio Supreme Court and has a primary practice in Ohio. The ordinary statute contains a specific alternative to Ohio legal residency for that attorney connection. The person still obtains the notary commission and meets the applicable conditions. Bar admission alone is not the electronic state application or office oath.

sections.heading: Apply the actual attorney exceptions
sections.body: For first commissioning after September 20, 2019, ordinary education remains required while the ordinary test is exempted. The application criminal-record-check exemption is also specified. These provisions do not remove every professional responsibility. A disqualifying offense during the term can still trigger the stated reporting and revocation provisions, including for an attorney.

sections.heading: Reassess online eligibility
sections.body: The online statute requires the online notary to be an Ohio resident and physically within Ohio when performing the act. The ordinary nonresident-attorney connection does not replace those RON conditions. A vendor account, Ohio client or Ohio office mailing address does not establish where the notary actually lives and performs the online session.

sections.heading: Track the online expiration
sections.body: Ordinary attorney authority continues while its stated Ohio connection, good standing and no-revocation conditions hold. Attorney online authorization nevertheless ends at the earlier of five years or the ordinary authority ending. The current online renewal table also calls for its separate approved hour. Continuing ordinary status should not be used as a reason to ignore the online expiration date.

faqs.q: Does ordinary nonresident attorney eligibility establish RON residency?
faqs.a: No. Online authority has its separate Ohio-resident condition.

faqs.q: Does attorney online authorization continue indefinitely?
faqs.a: It has the separate statutory five-year-or-earlier ending rule.

articles.keyword: Ohio fees follow acts and sessions instead of a signature multiplier
articles.title: Ohio fees follow acts and sessions instead of a signature multiplier
articles.description: Apply the current basic ceilings and the separate additional-charge rules.
articles.h1: Ohio fees follow acts and sessions instead of a signature multiplier
articles.lede: A group signing and a failed identity attempt can raise different fee questions in the same appointment.

sections.heading: Choose the correct basic category
sections.body: An Akron online session includes several principals signing a record. Ohio's current statute permits up to thirty dollars for an online notarization and five dollars for an act that is not online. The notary cannot add the ordinary basic fee to the online basic fee for the same act. The proper category follows the actual notarial method used.

sections.heading: Avoid the signature multiplier
sections.body: The statutory basic fees are not calculated per signature. Counting visible autographs on a document therefore does not by itself establish a lawful multiplied bill. Separate the actual acts from the number of signatures and apply the statutory structure, instead of importing a per-signature pricing rule from another state or a private provider's sales materials.

sections.heading: Apply the technology session unit
sections.body: The technology fee is up to ten dollars total for an online session and may apply even when the act is not completed, such as an identity-process failure. Several questions or repeated attempts within one session do not create a new cap for every attempt. The permission to charge despite failure also does not permit reporting a false identity pass.

sections.heading: Address any travel independently
sections.body: A reasonable travel fee must be agreed by the principal and notary before the act. It remains a separate condition from the basic and technology charges. Education provider fees and state application fees belong to becoming or remaining a notary, and should not be confused with the customer-service fee categories prescribed for this appointment.

faqs.q: Can the five-dollar basic fee be added to the online basic fee?
faqs.a: The statute prohibits stacking those basic categories.

faqs.q: Is ten dollars the technology cap for each KBA question?
faqs.a: No. It is the total technology cap per online session.

articles.keyword: A broken Ohio online connection restarts incomplete work
articles.title: A broken Ohio online connection restarts incomplete work
articles.description: Use the current rule's restart and refusal conditions through the whole session.
articles.h1: A broken Ohio online connection restarts incomplete work
articles.lede: A previous identity result does not allow an online act to continue through a compromised connection.

sections.heading: Identify the interruption
sections.body: A Cleveland principal passes the identity process but loses the audio-video link before the act is finished. Rule 111:6-1-05 addresses a participant exiting, a broken link or quality degradation that the notary believes compromises completion. These events are considered before assuming that a saved screen can substitute for the lawful live interaction.

sections.heading: Restart the stated components
sections.body: The rule requires restarting identity authentication and any incomplete online acts from the beginning. It does not say that collecting a second fee permits skipping the restarted procedure. The notary uses the renewed live session to complete the actual lawful appearance, identity and act rather than treating a prior result as proof that every later requirement is satisfied.

sections.heading: Check the refusal grounds
sections.body: The notary refuses when identity or transmission security cannot be verified, the principal's signature cannot attach to the electronic document or the technology cannot make the act tamper-evident. A customer waiver cannot add a missing technical capability. The notary evaluates whether the actual system can support completion before executing the certificate.

sections.heading: Preserve the completed session evidence
sections.body: The electronic journal and required recording describe the actual online procedure. Statutory safeguards include tamper-evident authenticated records, backups and protection from unauthorized access. A final seal screenshot cannot replace the communication on which identity was established or the accurate account of how the completed notarization occurred after the interruption.

faqs.q: Does reconnecting permit automatic continuation from the last screen?
faqs.a: The rule requires restarting identity authentication and incomplete acts.

faqs.q: May a customer waive an insecure connection?
faqs.a: The mandatory refusal condition still applies.

articles.keyword: Ohio online journal access has specific-entry and attorney safeguards
articles.title: Ohio online journal access has specific-entry and attorney safeguards
articles.description: Assess the request scope before releasing any part of the archive.
articles.h1: Ohio online journal access has specific-entry and attorney safeguards
articles.lede: A lawful journal request concerns identified entries and does not automatically transfer control of the journal.

sections.heading: Require the specific request
sections.body: A person asks a nonattorney Ohio online notary for an entry. The ordinary route requires a signed tangible or electronic request identifying month, year, record type and principal. The notary retains possession and control and shows or copies only the specified entries. One request should not become a chance to browse unrelated customers' transactions.

sections.heading: Record the access event
sections.body: The statute requires a separate new journal entry explaining the request circumstances and any related copy certification. It also permits the online notary to certify copies made from that journal, despite the ordinary direct-copy restriction. These provisions work together with the limited-entry access conditions instead of opening the archive without records of the release.

sections.heading: Apply the attorney rule
sections.body: An attorney authorized for online acts permits the stated ordinary access only to a principal in the transaction or someone acting on a principal's behalf, and can deny based on attorney-client privilege. The special deposited-attorney-journal provision likewise limits the eligible requester. The requester's interest in a document does not itself establish the necessary principal relationship.

sections.heading: Keep official process distinct
sections.body: The chapter provides official-investigation and court or state access routes, with the attorney privilege-objection qualification. A reasonable explainable belief of criminal or inappropriate purpose also supports the specified ordinary access denial. Identify which route actually applies before treating a customer request, an official investigation and a privilege claim as the same procedural event.

faqs.q: May a qualifying requester take the whole journal home?
faqs.a: No. The notary retains control and provides only specified entries.

faqs.q: Can a stranger automatically inspect an attorney-notary's entries?
faqs.a: The special rule requires the principal relationship and preserves privilege.

articles.keyword: Ohio online renewal begins a new electronic journal
articles.title: Ohio online renewal begins a new electronic journal
articles.description: Plan the archive transfer and receiving retention duties before authority ends.
articles.h1: Ohio online renewal begins a new electronic journal
articles.lede: A continuing vendor subscription does not decide the statutory journal lifecycle.

sections.heading: Track the authorization date
sections.body: An Ohio online notary approaches renewal while the provider dashboard still allows entries. The statute ties journal responsibilities to legal authorization, with separate attorney and nonattorney authorization clocks. Check the actual state authorization date instead of treating account availability as evidence that the notary's authority and journal period have automatically continued.

sections.heading: Start the new record period
sections.body: On effective renewal, section 147.65 requires a new electronic journal. The earlier record does not disappear because a fresh journal is opened. Its required transfer and preservation are handled through the statutory structure. The notary distinguishes beginning new entries under renewed authority from keeping access to records created under the preceding authorization.

sections.heading: Use an approved destination
sections.body: On the stated expiration transfer, transmit the electronic journal to the Secretary or an approved repository and inform the Secretary of the repository location when applicable. The receiving Secretary or repository has the ten-year retention duty identified in the subsection. An ordinary employer demand for the archive is different from the approved agreed repository arrangement allowed by law.

sections.heading: Provide usable access and continuity
sections.body: The related security section addresses access instructions and transfer after resignation, revocation, expiration without renewal, death or adjudicated incompetence. A person holding the instructions supplies them as required. Closing an account should therefore account for accessible lawful preservation, instead of treating cancellation as permission to delete all recordings and journal entries.

faqs.q: Is the same journal simply continued after effective online renewal?
faqs.a: The statute directs beginning a new electronic journal.

faqs.q: Does any employer automatically qualify to retain the archive?
faqs.a: The statute distinguishes ordinary retention from an approved agreed repository arrangement.

articles.keyword: Ohio identity quiz retries have an allowance and a later restriction
articles.title: Ohio identity quiz retries have an allowance and a later restriction
articles.description: Read both timing paragraphs before scheduling another attempt.
articles.h1: Ohio identity quiz retries have an allowance and a later restriction
articles.lede: The current rule's KBA specifications govern a principal's identity assessment separately from the notary's licensing exam.

sections.heading: Use the actual assessment specification
sections.body: For the prescribed dynamic KBA route, Ohio requires at least five personal-history or identity questions with at least five choices per question. At least eighty percent are correct within two minutes. A five-question quiz therefore needs four correct answers. These numbers should not be presented as the ordinary statewide commissioning exam specification.

sections.heading: Apply the retry allowance
sections.body: The rule states that after a first failure the individual may retake twice within forty-eight hours. A retake replaces at least forty percent of the prior questions, which means at least two on a five-question quiz. This is a structured identity assessment, so repeating the same unchanged question set does not meet the stated replacement condition.

sections.heading: Apply the second-failure restriction too
sections.body: Another paragraph bars retry with the same notary or the same proofing third person within twenty-four hours after the second failed attempt. The overall allowance does not delete this more specific timing restriction. Switching only the notary while immediately using the same service does not avoid the service-related condition in that paragraph.

sections.heading: Keep answers separate from the notary
sections.body: The notary must not see or record the questions or answers. The provider also has credential-analysis, image-capture and result-output obligations separate from the quiz. Passing KBA alone cannot replace the remaining identity components, live communication or the actual notarial act. A failed process can have its own lawful technology-fee treatment without changing the recorded identity outcome.

faqs.q: Can changing only the notary always permit immediate retry after a second failure?
faqs.a: No. The same proofing-service restriction also applies.

faqs.q: May the notary save the quiz answers to coach the signer?
faqs.a: The rule prohibits seeing or recording the questions or answers.

articles.keyword: An Ohio electronic document can be notarized in the same room
articles.title: An Ohio electronic document can be notarized in the same room
articles.description: Distinguish electronic execution from an online appearance and the authenticator exception.
articles.h1: An Ohio electronic document can be notarized in the same room
articles.lede: A tablet or electronic seal does not by itself establish that an Ohio notarization is remote.

sections.heading: Identify the participants' actual location
sections.body: A Columbus signer and ordinary commissioned notary share the same room and execute an electronic record. Section 147.591 permits electronic signatures and seals for this physical-presence route. It is distinct from the online method in which the principal appears through live two-way audiovisual technology and the notary has separate online authorization.

sections.heading: Describe the actual method
sections.body: The certificate includes the appropriate indication of physical-presence electronic performance or online appearance. The rule provides corresponding statement forms. A certificate should not say that a signer appeared online merely because the record is digital. Likewise, physical-presence wording cannot be used to describe someone who participated only through a remote link.

sections.heading: Secure electronic execution
sections.body: The electronic seal and signature follow the applicable statutory security provisions. The electronic attachment permits independent verification and makes later document changes evident. The same-room route does not turn a freely pasted logo into a secure notarial signature or authorize a coworker to use the notary's personal electronic credentials.

sections.heading: Recognize the special later paper route
sections.body: For the particular printed-electronic-document recording procedure, the authenticator certificate has its own condition: it cannot be electronically signed or notarized, including through an online system. The source record's electronic status therefore does not determine every later certificate's execution method. Check the specific stage and statutory role being requested.

faqs.q: Does every electronic document require remote appearance?
faqs.a: No. Section 147.591 permits the physical-presence electronic route.

faqs.q: Can the special authenticator certificate always be electronic too?
faqs.a: Its specific subsection prohibits electronic signing and notarization.

articles.keyword: Ohio representative acknowledgment leaves legal-validity opinions separate
articles.title: Ohio representative acknowledgment leaves legal-validity opinions separate
articles.description: Identify the agent or officer while staying within the nonattorney notarial role.
articles.h1: Ohio representative acknowledgment leaves legal-validity opinions separate
articles.lede: Acknowledging a representative execution does not automatically include a legal opinion on the source of authority.

sections.heading: Identify the human representative
sections.body: A Cincinnati attorney-in-fact appears to acknowledge a record for a principal. The notary knows or obtains satisfactory evidence that the appearing person is the individual named in the instrument or certificate. An impressive title does not establish the human identity, and the principal's absence does not mean the notary identifies only the represented person's name on paper.

sections.heading: Record the correct capacity
sections.body: The representative acknowledges proper authority and execution as the represented person's act for the stated purpose. The statutory short form distinguishes the attorney-in-fact and principal. Corporate, LLC, partnership and other roles have their respective forms and meanings. Accurate role wording describes the execution instead of treating every representative as signing personally for themselves.

sections.heading: Avoid the prohibited validity determination
sections.body: Section 147.141 restricts a nonattorney notary from determining legal validity of a power of attorney or another representative-capacity document. The representative's acknowledgment of authority and the notary's legal opinion about the document are different acts. The commission does not confer an Ohio law license to decide that issue for the customer.

sections.heading: Screen the notary's own position
sections.body: The chapter separately defines conflicts through direct interests beyond authorized fees and named-party roles. A notary who is individually named as trustee or a transaction party does not eliminate that conflict by using an otherwise accurate representative certificate for someone else. Examine the officer's own position before performing the ceremony and certifying the completed event.

faqs.q: Does attorney-in-fact mean the agent is an Ohio lawyer?
faqs.a: No. It describes the representative role in the transaction.

faqs.q: Does the acknowledgment guarantee legal validity of the power?
faqs.a: The nonattorney notary does not acquire that legal-opinion authority through acknowledgment.
